stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A mass hangs from a spring. Adjust the mass $m$ and the spring stiffness $k$, then press CONFIRM to log each configuration. Watch how the elongation $\Delta L$ changes as you vary $m$ and $k$.
stages.concept: At rest, two collinear forces act on the mass: weight $P = m \cdot g$ (down) and spring reaction $R = k \cdot \Delta L$ (up). Equilibrium requires $\sum F_{\text{ext}} = 0$, so $R = P$ and $\Delta L_{\text{eq}} = \dfrac{m g}{k}$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Match each highlighted target elongation $\Delta L$. Tune $m$ and $k$ until the spring settles at the target, then press CONFIRM. Hit all three targets to advance.
stages.concept: Two DOFs, one relation: $\Delta L_{\text{eq}} = \dfrac{m g}{k}$. Any $(m, k)$ satisfying this reaches the same $\Delta L$ — double $m$ and double $k$ leaves $\Delta L$ unchanged.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The force arrows and force readouts are hidden. Each target shows the required elongation $\Delta L$ and the spring stiffness $k$. Compute the mass $m$ that produces equilibrium at that $\Delta L$, set the sliders, then CONFIRM. You have one submission per target — plan on paper before you commit.
stages.concept: Equilibrium of two collinear forces: $\sum F = 0 \Rightarrow R = P \Rightarrow k \cdot \Delta L = m g$. Solve for the unknown: $m = \dfrac{k \cdot \Delta L}{g}$ and $P = k \cdot \Delta L$.

labels.tip1: adjust m, adjust k, then CONFIRM
labels.tip2: match each ΔL target, CONFIRM to lock it in
labels.tip3: compute m = k·ΔL/g on paper, then CONFIRM
labels.peek_tip_balance: At equilibrium R = P, so k·ΔL = m·g. Solve m = k·ΔL/g.
labels.peek_tip_double: Doubling k halves ΔL for the same mass. Doubling m doubles ΔL for the same spring.
labels.peek_tip_units: Keep units clean: m in kg, k in N/m, ΔL in m, g ≈ 9.81 m/s². Then P and R come out in N.

1.1: Drag the mass slider left and right — watch the spring stretch.
1.2: The vertical slider on the right sets spring stiffness k. Stiffer spring = shorter elongation for the same weight.
1.3: Press CONFIRM after each change to log the configuration. Try at least two very different masses.

2.1: Read the target ΔL on the ruler beside the spring. Tune m and k until the spring settles there.
2.2: For a given target ΔL, any (m, k) pair with m/k = ΔL/g works. There are infinitely many valid pairs.
2.3: If the spring is too short, either increase m or decrease k. Confirm only when the mass sits on the target line.

3.1: The target shows ΔL and k. Everything you need to compute m is on screen.
3.2: Apply the equilibrium condition: k·ΔL = m·g. Solve for m before touching the sliders.
3.3: m = k·ΔL/g. Compute it, dial it in, CONFIRM. One shot per target — do the math first.
